patients.label: 67-year-old man with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes presenting with loss of consciousness and necrotizing otitis externa with skull base osteomyelitis and cranial nerve palsies

identity_evidence.quote: a 67-year-old gentleman with insulin-dependent type 2 diabetes mellitus

attribution_limitations: The discharge CRP is printed as 1.4 g/L while the same sentence says inflammatory markers were back to normal; read literally, 1.4 g/L would be far above the admission value of 73 mg/L, so the printed unit or value conflicts with the normal statement.

The Carney staging table lists a positive Tc-99m bone scan as part of stages 2 and 3, but no bone scan is reported for this patient; Stage 3b is stated by the authors from multiple cranial nerve involvement.
Complex NOE is hedged by the authors ("likely", "consistent with", "possible") rather than stated as definite.
It is not stated whether "bilateral" applies to otitis media and mastoiditis as well as otitis externa.
The sentence on reduced hearing names the "affected ear" without restating its side, and the cranial nerve table reports gross bilateral hearing reduction.
The timing of the diabetic ketoacidosis admission, of the ENT-known ear disease and of the earlier histology is described only as recent or known, without dates.

claims.text: A 67-year-old man with a 15-year history of insulin-treated type 2 diabetes with suboptimal control, essential hypertension, chronic pancreatitis and a 45-pack-year smoking history presented to the emergency department with loss of consciousness and a blood glucose of 2.6 mmol/L, and regained consciousness after the hypoglycemia was corrected. An obvious right facial nerve palsy had lasted three weeks, and he was known to ENT with ear disease and a recent diabetic ketoacidosis admission.

claims.text: He had persistent right ear pain, minimal discharge and reduced hearing, previously treated with oral co-amoxiclav and ear spray. Examination and a full cranial nerve examination found multiple cranial nerve abnormalities, and the ear swab grew ciprofloxacin-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. CRP and white cell count were raised, CT showed destruction of the right petrous apex and skull base, and MRI showed extensive right necrotizing otitis externa with skull base osteomyelitis and granulation tissue at the osseocartilaginous junction; Doppler ultrasound excluded thrombosis.
